questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist receives an advisory letter from the Board after a complaint review. A credentialing form later asks whether that Board outcome was formal disciplinary action. Based on the classification of the Board action itself, which response is most accurate?

choices.text: Yes. Any written Board communication resolving a complaint is formal discipline.
No. An advisory letter may be retained in Board files but is not itself formal disciplinary action.
Yes. An advisory letter is the same disciplinary category as probation.
No. The letter has no regulatory significance and may be treated as though it never existed.
Yes. The letter automatically suspends the pharmacist's registration until the next renewal.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist recognizes that a substance-use condition may affect safe practice and asks about the current state recovery-and-monitoring pathway. Which statements accurately describe URAMP? Select all that apply.

choices.text: It is a confidential, voluntary recovery and monitoring program available to BHPL-licensed health professionals.
The former pharmacy PSUD program transitioned into URAMP when URAMP launched.
Admission guarantees that the Board must dismiss every pending complaint involving the participant.
A licensing board may refer a licensee to URAMP, and admission can involve an individualized rehabilitation plan.
URAMP is available only after the Board has imposed a formal suspension.

questions.stem: A pharmacist offers counseling on a new prescription. The patient says, "I have taken it before and do not want counseling today." The prescription is otherwise ready to dispense. What Massachusetts documentation step best addresses the refusal?

choices.text: Record the patient's failure to accept the counseling offer in the patient profile, prescription signature log, or another appropriate record system.
Require the patient to sign a Board-specific refusal form before the prescription can be released.
Document a complete counseling session because a refusal cannot be recorded as a refusal.
Delete the counseling offer from the record because no counseling occurred.
Contact the prescriber and obtain authorization to waive counseling.

questions.stem: A community pharmacy receives manufacturer-packaged tablets that are identified as hazardous drugs. The pharmacy will store and dispense the intact tablets but will not compound them. A manager says hazardous-drug standards are irrelevant because no compounding will occur. Which approach is most accurate?

choices.text: Treat the shipment as ordinary inventory because hazardous-drug standards begin only when a dosage form is compounded.
Apply current hazardous-drug handling standards to the applicable receipt, storage, dispensing, and disposal activities even though the pharmacy is not compounding the tablets.
Apply sterile-compounding cleanroom rules to every intact hazardous tablet before it may be dispensed.
Return every hazardous drug to the wholesaler because community pharmacies may not possess hazardous drugs.
Follow hazardous-drug controls only if the prescription is for an employee of the pharmacy.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy plans to mail a temperature-sensitive prescription using a common carrier. The proposed packaging cannot reasonably maintain the product's labeled storage conditions during the expected transit. What should the pharmacy do?

choices.text: Ship it because use of a common carrier transfers responsibility for product stability to the carrier.
Ship it if the patient agrees to accept the risk of temperature excursion.
Use a packing and transportation method that protects medication integrity and stability before sending the prescription.
Remove the labeled storage directions so the carrier is not responsible for them.
Convert the order to an in-store pickup without telling the patient.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts drug store pharmacy holds its ordinary pharmacy license but has never obtained a sterile compounding pharmacy license. It wants to begin preparing patient-specific sterile ophthalmic preparations on site. Which statement best describes the licensure issue?

choices.text: The ordinary drug store license is sufficient whenever each preparation is patient-specific.
The pharmacy may begin immediately and seek a sterile-compounding license only if the Board later inspects it.
The pharmacy needs the applicable sterile compounding pharmacy licensure before engaging in this sterile compounding activity.
Sterile compounding is permitted without additional licensure when no Schedule II-V drug is used.
Sterile compounding licensure applies only to out-of-state pharmacies shipping into Massachusetts.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy proposes a non-sterile preparation that requires specialized training, a dedicated controlled environment, and techniques presenting elevated complexity. The manager concludes that an ordinary drug store license is enough because the final preparation is not sterile. Which response best applies?

choices.text: Agree; every non-sterile preparation falls outside specialty pharmacy licensure.
Require a sterile compounding pharmacy license because any complex preparation is treated as sterile.
Evaluate the activity under the separate complex non-sterile compounding category and obtain the applicable license before performing that regulated activity.
Proceed under ordinary licensure as long as the preparation contains no hazardous ingredient.
Proceed under ordinary licensure if the pharmacy limits the preparation to one patient per day.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is appropriately licensed for a proposed compounding activity and plans to compound a drug that is hazardous under the applicable standards. Which principles should the pharmacist apply? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Continue to follow the sterile or non-sterile compounding requirements applicable to the preparation.
Apply the current hazardous-drug handling requirements that govern the hazardous ingredient and compounding process.
Treat hazardous-drug status as replacing all other compounding requirements.
Ignore hazardous-drug controls if the prescription is patient-specific.
Use the fact that the pharmacy has a compounding license as proof that no additional hazardous-drug operational controls apply.

questions.stem: A patient asks a Massachusetts pharmacy to compound a non-hazardous version of a commercially available drug solely because the compounded version would cost less. The commercially available product otherwise meets the patient's needs, and the prescriber identifies no patient-specific clinical difference. Which statement best applies to the statutory compounding analysis?

choices.text: Lower price alone establishes the patient-specific significant difference needed for compounding the commercially available product.
The pharmacy may treat price as the significant difference only when the patient signs a waiver.
A difference in price alone does not constitute the patient-specific significant difference contemplated by the Massachusetts compounding definition.
The pharmacy must reclassify the preparation as sterile because it uses a commercially available product.
The pharmacy may compound solely for price whenever the quantity is less than a 30-day supply.

questions.stem: Two separately owned Massachusetts pharmacies want one pharmacy to perform central-fill services for prescriptions originating at the other. They have compatible secure systems but no common ownership. Which governance step is central to making this shared-service structure permissible under current Board policy?

choices.text: They must become commonly owned because unrelated pharmacies may not participate in shared pharmacy services.
They should use a written agreement that defines the shared services and each participating pharmacy's responsibilities, while satisfying the policy's other safeguards.
They may proceed without an agreement if both Managers of Record give oral approval.
They should transfer every prescription to the filling pharmacy and stop treating the arrangement as central fill.
They need a patient-specific court order for each prescription processed through the arrangement.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts drug store pharmacy license was issued in March 2026. The owner is preparing the facility's renewal calendar and is comparing it with the pharmacist staff's personal registration cycle. When does this drug store pharmacy license expire under the facility-license rule?

choices.text: December 31, 2026, because every pharmacy license expires at the end of the year of issuance.
March 2027, exactly one year after issuance.
December 31, 2027, the next odd-numbered-year December 31 following issuance.
December 31, 2028, because pharmacy facilities use the same even-year cycle as pharmacists' personal registrations.
It has no fixed expiration date as long as a Manager of Record remains employed.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy completed its routine annual self-inspection three months ago. It now relocates to a new address, and a Board inspector arrives without prior notice shortly afterward. Which statements are accurate? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The relocation triggers another Board-tool self-inspection within the regulatory timeframe even though the annual self-inspection was recent.
The Board may inspect the licensed pharmacy without prior notice.
The pharmacy may decline to provide requested pharmacy records because the inspection was unannounced.
The recent annual self-inspection prevents another self-inspection from being required during the same calendar year.
The pharmacy should provide documents requested by the Board or its designee in connection with the inspection.

questions.stem: During an investigation, the Board finds conditions at a pharmacy that present an immediate and serious threat to public health and safety. Waiting for a final adjudicatory decision would leave the unsafe operation in place. Which Board response is most consistent with the Massachusetts disciplinary framework?

choices.text: The Board must wait for a final disciplinary hearing before restricting the pharmacy's operation or affected products.
The Board may use an appropriate summary cease-and-desist or quarantine mechanism, subject to the regulation's subsequent review procedures.
The Board can act only against the individual pharmacist and has no emergency authority directed at the pharmacy or affected products.
The Board must convert the matter into an advisory letter because emergency action cannot be disciplinary.
The Board may permanently revoke the pharmacy license without any procedural review because the threat is serious.

questions.stem: The Manager of Record of a Massachusetts retail pharmacy plans a six-week medical leave. The dates are known in advance. Which steps are required for this planned absence under 247 CMR 9.23? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Appoint a Board-registered Interim Manager before the planned absence begins.
Have the Manager of Record perform a controlled-substance inventory before leaving, signed by the Manager of Record and Interim Manager.
Wait five days after the leave begins before deciding whether an Interim Manager is needed.
Immediately file a permanent change-of-Manager application solely because the planned leave exceeds 30 days.
Allow the pharmacy to operate without a designated interim manager as long as another pharmacist is on each shift.

questions.stem: A pharmacy filled a prescription, but the patient never picked it up and the medication never left the pharmacy's control. Staff want to return the tablets to inventory by pouring them back into the manufacturer's stock bottle. What is the appropriate Massachusetts approach?

choices.text: The medication cannot be returned to stock once the prescription has been prepared and a patient-specific label has been applied.
The medication may be returned to stock under pharmacy policy in an appropriately identified return-to-stock container, without commingling it with manufacturer stock.
The medication may be poured into the manufacturer stock bottle because it never left the pharmacy or reached the patient.
The medication must be dispensed to another patient promptly or destroyed because prepared prescriptions cannot remain available for later reuse.
The medication may be returned to the manufacturer stock bottle after the first patient identifying information is removed from pharmacy records.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist receives a prescription for a brand-name biological product. The prescriber has not prohibited substitution. The pharmacy has a less expensive FDA-licensed biosimilar, but FDA has not determined that product to be interchangeable with the prescribed biologic. May the pharmacist substitute that biosimilar under Massachusetts' statutory biologic-substitution authority without obtaining new prescriber authorization?

choices.text: Yes, because every FDA-licensed biosimilar is automatically interchangeable for pharmacy substitution.
Yes, because the absence of a prescriber prohibition is the only condition Massachusetts imposes.
No. The statutory substitution pathway requires an FDA determination that the substitute is interchangeable with the prescribed biological product.
No, because Massachusetts prohibits pharmacist substitution of any biological product.
Yes, but only if the patient waives notification to the prescriber.
